title: U.S.-Registered Drone Detected at Site of Suspected CIA Boat Strike
author: Camila Lourdes Galarza
content:

_An eyewitness watches the Negra Francisca boat burning on March 17, 2026 near
the Galapagos Islands. Photo: Darwin Flores-Pico._

QUITO, Ecuador--In the hours after a mysterious attack on an Ecuadorian
fishing boat near the Galapagos Islands on March 17, a drone registered to
U.S. defense contractor Shield AI was hovering just 500 meters from the
burning vessel, La Negra Francisca, according to a review of flight tracking
data by Drop Site News. This represents the first known vehicle to arrive at
the site of the strike.

The unattributed bombing of three Ecuadorian fishing boats in January and
March, and the subsequent abduction and torture of 36 fishermen, was first
[reported by Drop Site](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/rare-survivors-of-
pacific-boat-strikes) in April. Last week, The Washington Post, building on
Drop Site's [ongoing investigation](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/prosecutor-
investigating-ecuador-boat-strikes-murdered), reported that the attacks were
part of a covert CIA operation.

According to flight and vessel tracking data from Radar 24 and Global Fishing
Watch, the drone was a [V-BAT model](https://shield.ai/v-bat/), primarily used
for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance, but capable of carrying a
weapons payload and switching its signal on and off to avoid detection.

The Shield AI drone matches the fishermen's descriptions of the drones that
circled their boats before the bombing, and bears the same red and green
lights eyewitnesses reported seeing as they photographed the explosion.

Shield AI did not respond to a request for comment.

The CEO of Shield AI, Brandon Tseng, has [publicly
stated](https://truthout.org/articles/venture-capitalists-are-using-profits-
from-genocide-to-fund-ai-powered-weapons/) that the U.S. Coast Guard and Navy
are using V-BAT drones "to interdict and destroy billions of dollars' worth of
drugs that were headed for the United States of America." In 2024, the U.S.
Coast Guard signed a $198 million [contract](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-
releases/shield-ais-v-bat-selected-for-198-million-contract-to-provide-us-
coast-guard-with-maritime-unmanned-aircraft-system-services-302187333.html)
with Shield AI for V-BAT drones; in April 2026, Shield AI announced it had
received an [$800 million contract](https://shield.ai/shield-ai-selected-by-u-
s-navy-to-compete-for-800m-in-isr-services-with-v-bat/) for V-BAT drones from
the U.S. Navy.

No drugs were found on any of the three fishing boats [investigated by Drop
Site](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/prosecutor-investigating-ecuador-boat-
strikes-murdered)--the Negra Francisca, Don Maca, and Fiorella--all of which
were searched and cleared by Ecuadorian coast guard personnel prior to the
strikes.

Last month[, Drop Site published NASA thermal imagery consistent with an
explosion](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/prosecutor-investigating-ecuador-
boat-strikes-murdered) at coordinates 1.5822°N, 87.6958W°, recorded at 1:02
p.m., the time fishermen say they were hit, and in the location where their
transponder stopped broadcasting.

Tracking data suggests that the drone launched from a nearby boat on March 17,
seven hours after the strike on La Negra Francisca and then circled near the
site, its signal disappearing and reappearing. Ascending and descending
patterns of movement indicate that the drone may have been landing on a boat
and then resuming its flights.

Drop Site previously [reported](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/prosecutor-
investigating-ecuador-boat-strikes-murdered) that vessel tracking data showed
a U.S. Coast Guard cutter leaving a Galapagos military base a day before the
Negra Francisca bombing--despite claiming it only deployed the cutter as a
post-incident rescue effort. The Coast Guard vessel's signal went dark and
later appeared in Central American waters 24 hours before the fishermen were
placed in El Salvador's custody.

Video recordings, taken by eyewitnesses to the bombing, show the U.S. Coast
Guard patrolling in the aftermath of the airstrike. Drop Site asked the U.S.
Coast Guard in June to account for the cutter's movements after its signal
went dark. The Coast Guard responded that it "does not disclose cutter
movements during law enforcement missions for operational security."

In June, the U.S. Coast Guard told [The
Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jun/13/ecuador-fishing-boats-
us-strikes) it deployed its Bertholf cutter for a search-and-rescue operation
after receiving a Mayday alert, contradicting prior statements by the U.S.
Southern Command, which oversees maritime operations in the Pacific, that it
had no knowledge of any U.S. involvement in the incidents. To date, the U.S.
Coast Guard has not acknowledged using drones in its purported rescue efforts.

The U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Southern Command, and the Central Intelligence
Agency did not respond to questions for this article.

While flight tracking data is recorded in UTC, dating the drone activity as
March 18, in Galapagos time (UTC-06:00) both the strike and the subsequent
drone activity occurred on March 17.

Shield AI, a San Diego-based defense contractor, builds fighter jets and
drones powered and piloted by artificial intelligence. The company was founded
in 2016 with [$1 million in seed
funding](https://www.defenseone.com/technology/2016/09/special-operators-are-
getting-new-autonomous-tactical-drone/131431/) from the[ Pentagon's Defense
Innovation Unit](https://www.diu.mil/) and[ the Naval Special Warfare
Command](https://www.privacyinternational.org/report/5721/dual-use-tech-
shield-ai-example). The Israeli military has
[reportedly](https://www.politico.com/news/2023/11/25/israel-hamas-war-ai-
weapons-00128550) used the company's self-piloting drones for close quarters
combat. V-BAT drones are also used by the [Ukrainian
military](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/american-made-technology-guiding-
ukraines-strikes-into-russia/) to identify Russian targets, as part of larger
drone strike operations.

###### Video of the burning fishing boat La Negra Francisca, taken by Darwin
Flores-Pico, after the March 17, 2026 attack.

Last week, the [New York
Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/12/world/americas/ecuador-fishing-boat-
strikes.html) and the [Washington
Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/investigations/2026/08/13/covert-cia-
program-said-be-behind-mysterious-attacks-galpagos-boats/) corroborated much
of Drop Site's original investigation of the attacks. In addition, the Times
reported that a patrol plane flew from a military base in El Salvador in the
direction of the three boats prior to each of the attacks. The Post identified
that plane as FENIX 701, a Cessna business jet equipped with surveillance
equipment operating out of Ilopango International Airport, which served as a
hub for CIA operations during the Contra War against the Sandinista government
of Nicaragua. The plane is registered to a company with virtually no digital
footprint that lists its address as a mailbox inside a Virginia UPS store.

The FENIX 701 stopped broadcasting its signal well before reaching any of the
boats and returned to base hours before the actual strikes, according to
flight data.

The fishermen, like the airplane, eventually wound up in El Salvador. As Drop
Site previously [reported](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/rare-survivors-of-
pacific-boat-strikes), men from the Negra Francisca and Don Maca boats were
taken hostage by "gringo" gunmen in U.S. military uniforms who they say
hooded, handcuffed, and starved them for eight days aboard their U.S.-flagged
ship before turning them over to El Salvador's navy hundreds of miles away
from home.

Since September 2025, the U.S. military has carried out over 66 strikes on
vessels in the Caribbean and the eastern Pacific, killing at least 221, as
part of Operation Southern Spear. The Trump administration has been boastful
and unapologetic about this extrajudicial killing spree, which raises the
question of why it would also run a covert CIA operation alongside it, as the
Washington Post reported. There is precedent for such parallel operations,
however. In April, for example, it was revealed that CIA agents were secretly
working joint counter-narcotics raids with local agents in Mexico's Chihuahua
state without informing President Claudia Sheinbaum--despite her
administration's bilateral efforts with U.S. forces.

"We certainly do have cases in which one part of the U.S. government is doing
something covertly while another part is doing something overtly," Vincent
Bevins, author of "The Jakarta Method _,_ "__ a historical examination of the
CIA's Cold War operations, and editor of [North South
Notes](https://www.northsouthnotes.org/), told Drop Site.

"That covert operation might be doing the same thing in a different way. It
might be doing something similar and related," Bevins added. "Even, at cross
purposes, to some extent, with the official government line or official
government policy….There are also cases where the only explanation is
institutional chaos or poor planning."

## **A Community Under Siege**

In June, Alexandra Bravo, a prosecutor investigating the U.S. strikes, was
[shot dead](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/prosecutor-investigating-ecuador-
boat-strikes-murdered) in the coastal city of Manta, the home port of the
three fishing boats. U.S. troops have been deployed in Manta since December
2025, and the return of a de facto U.S. military base there--originally
outlawed by the 2007 constitution and again ratified by 60% of Ecuadorian
voters last November--evokes painful memories for residents who have not
forgotten why it was banned in the first place: the U.S. publicly and brazenly
[sinking fishing ships
off](https://www.wola.org/sites/default/files/downloadable/Andes/Ecuador/past/March%202007%20Manta%20Memo.pdf)
the coast of Manta.

Ecuador is under its 23rd [martial law
decree](https://www.primicias.ec/politica/presidente-daniel-noboa-renueva-
estado-excepcion-provincias-cantones-ecuador-130323/), which allows
authorities to raid homes and wiretap communications without a warrant, and
grants diplomatic immunity to all U.S. forces. President Daniel Noboa
justifies the stripping of civil liberties as a necessary part of his "war on
narcos."

The strikes and subsequent abductions left Jordi Flores, a young crewmember
aboard the Negra Francisca, with a severe foot injury and unable to work. Erik
Coello, a crewmember aboard the Don Maca, which was also struck in March,
suffers from 70% vision loss. And the families of the Fiorella, which vanished
in January, have been crushed by grief for their missing sons, husbands, and
fathers.

Maria Mero, whose husband Gabriel Aladino Mero Delgado and brother Jefferson
Ariel Mero Cueva both disappeared on the Fiorella, told Drop Site that her
mother-in-law died awaiting her son's return, falling into a deep depression
and ceasing to eat in the weeks leading up to her death. Maria's young
daughter was hospitalized from the anxiety of going seven months without
seeing her father. Gabriel's disappearance also left a void in the family's
finances. Without him, Maria said, the ordinary necessities of life--
groceries, her electricity bill, their daughter's school uniform--are
completely unaffordable.

"If the CIA or the United States or the El Salvador patrol or the president is
reading this," Maria said, "please, I beg you, return my husband, my brother,
and all the people who are with them."
